## Walkthrough The operator's `newDegradedInertia()` function now applies a 10-minute inertia condition for `StaticPodsDegradedConditionType` in addition to the existing `NodeControllerDegradedConditionType` handling. Repeated inertia condition construction was refactored into a new helper `inertiaForCondition`. A matching test case was added. ### Changes **Degraded Inertia Extension** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Static pods inertia and helper refactor**
`pkg/operator/starter.go`, `pkg/operator/starter_test.go`|Introduces `inertiaForCondition(cond, duration)` helper to build `status.InertiaCondition` with exact-match regex; applies it to both node-controller and static-pods degraded conditions (10-minute duration); adds a test case asserting the 10-minute duration for `StaticPodsDegradedConditionType`.| **Estimated code review effort:** 1 (Trivial) | ~5 minutes **Possibly related PRs** - [openshift/cluster-kube-apiserver-operator#2219](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-kube-apiserver-operator/pull/2219): Both PRs modify the same `newDegradedInertia()` logic in `pkg/operator/starter.go`/`starter_test.go` to configure inertia conditions via condition-type matchers. **Suggested labels:** `lgtm`, `approved` **Suggested reviewers:** `p0lyn0mial`, `ricardomaraschini`

starter_test.go is a plain Go unit test, so MicroShift compatibility rules don’t apply. | | Single Node Openshift (Sno) Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The only added test is a unit test in pkg/operator/starter_test.go, not a Ginkgo e2e test with cluster-topology assumptions. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | Only degraded-inertia logic and its test changed;
